Description: This course introduces students to the fundamental principles of electronics, including Ohm's Law, circuit analysis, semiconductor devices, and basic electronic measurements used in the industry.
LearningOutcomes: Apply Ohm's Law and Kirchhoff's laws to analyse DC and AC circuits.
Identify and describe the characteristics of common electronic components including resistors, capacitors, diodes, and transistors.
Use a multimeter and oscilloscope to measure and interpret electrical quantities in electronic circuits.

Description: Students develop practical skills in assembling, soldering, and testing electronic circuits from schematics, including PCB construction and fault-finding techniques.
LearningOutcomes: Assemble electronic circuits from schematic diagrams to a professional standard.
Apply correct soldering techniques for through-hole and surface mount components.
Test and fault-find assembled circuits using systematic diagnostic procedures.

Description: An introductory course covering the properties of timber, the safe use of hand and power woodworking tools, and the production of basic joints used in carpentry and joinery.
LearningOutcomes: Identify different timber species and describe their properties and suitability for various applications.
Safely operate hand and power woodworking tools to produce accurate timber components.
Construct common carpentry joints to acceptable trade standards.

Description: This elective course builds on carpentry fundamentals to teach students the design, construction, and finishing of wooden furniture items, with a focus on quality and marketability.
LearningOutcomes: Design and construct a basic furniture item to customer specifications.
Apply surface preparation and wood finishing techniques including staining, varnishing, and painting.
Evaluate furniture for quality and identify areas for improvement.

Description: An introductory course covering the operating principles of motor vehicle systems, workshop safety, and routine vehicle maintenance procedures applicable to common vehicle types in Zambia.
LearningOutcomes: Explain the operating principles of the main automotive systems: engine, transmission, steering, braking, and electrical.
Perform routine vehicle maintenance tasks safely and in accordance with manufacturer specifications.
Apply workshop safety rules and demonstrate proper use of automotive tools and equipment.

Description: This course covers engine disassembly, inspection, measurement, reconditioning, and reassembly procedures for petrol and diesel engines, with emphasis on precision measurement and quality.
LearningOutcomes: Disassemble and reassemble a petrol or diesel engine following correct procedures.
Measure engine components using precision instruments and compare results to manufacturer specifications.
Identify worn or defective engine components and recommend appropriate remedial action.

Description: This course provides a foundation in computer hardware, operating systems, productivity software, and internet use, equipping students with essential digital skills for technical and professional environments.
LearningOutcomes: Identify and describe the function of major computer hardware components and peripheral devices.
Use operating system features to manage files, settings, and applications effectively.
Create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations using standard office productivity software.

Description: Students are introduced to data networking concepts including the OSI model, IP addressing, LAN configuration, and network troubleshooting, providing a foundation for further study in IT.
LearningOutcomes: Explain the OSI and TCP/IP network models and describe the function of each layer.
Configure a basic local area network including IP addressing, switches, and wireless access points.
Troubleshoot common network connectivity problems using appropriate diagnostic tools.
